author: garyrong
content:
Parent frame P has two children, A and B, P calls child A first

- A creates a new slot. The state-gas charge spills into gas_left

- A returns successfully.

- P calls sibling child B, and B clears the slot created by A.

- As B has nothing borrowed from gasLeft, the refill ends up in state-gas reservoir

- B returns successfully, with state-gas reservoir being absorbed by P

- P has an outstanding state-gas charge that was funded from gas_left, but the state-reservoir is non-zero

author: chfast
content: yes. P should absorb B state-gas leftovers also in the LIFO order, but it doesn't currently. you can also similar scenario in the parent-child relationship (instead of A call, just parent sets the slot), but I stick with sibling child example because it matches ERC-4337: it is very likely that 2 user ops in the bundle will interact with the same contract.

author: chfast
content: However, **there is big gotcha** in this EIP we missed so far. See https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12265/changes#diff-d4b64f73fdb76107aedcb0c719102fc1f48a82129a1e1f220959aa9f7fa12fc1R473. It is no related to the proposed change, but the change exposes it more. With EIP-8037 `GAS` values are not monotonic any more. Specifically, `GAS` difference can produce nonsensical results.
